# Remediation Plan

### For SQL Injections (CWE-89):
Use prepared statements with parameterized queries instead of concatenating user-provided strings directly into database queries. Example:
```c++
// Instead of direct concatenation like this:
char* sql = strcat("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='", username);
// Use parameterized/prepared statement approach:
sqlite3_stmt* stmt;
const char* sql_safe = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=?";
sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, sql_safe, strlen(sql_safe), &stmt, NULL);
sqlite3_bind_text(stmt, 1, username, -1, SQLITE_STATIC); // bind securely
```

### For Directory Traversals (CWE-20):
Sanitize all incoming file paths; restrict read/write permissions strictly to designated locations. Validate file names against whitelists only when possible.
```cpp
#include <limits.h> // PATH_MAX
...
void safe_path(const char* base_dir, const char* relative_path){
    char resolved_path[PATH_MAX];
    if(!realpath(relative_path, resolved_path)) return;
    
    // Ensure resolved path starts from expected base dir
    bool valid = strncmp(resolved_path, base_dir, strlen(base_dir)) == 0 &&
                 resolved_path[strlen(base_dir)] == '/';
    if (!valid) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Access denied!");
        exit(1);
    }
}
```

### For Race Conditions (CWE-362):
Employ mutexes/semaphores around shared mutable state variables accessed simultaneously over multiple threads/processes.
```cpp
pthread_mutex_t lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

void thread_safe_operation(){
    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
    try{
        // Perform critical operation here
    } finally{
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    }
}
```
